name: Air-skin stent
subtitle: a stent blood cannot clot on

effects.effect: microscopic bumps make water bead up and roll off, carrying dirt away

effect: microscopic bumps make water bead up and roll off, carrying dirt away
how: After a stent props open a heart artery, patients take blood thinners for months or years, which cause dangerous bleeding, because platelets stick to the metal and form clots. A stent coated in microscopic water-repelling bumps holds a thin cushion of air against the blood, so platelets have nothing to cling to.
obstacle: Under blood pressure the trapped air dissolves within hours to days, after which the surface acts like plain metal.
why: Water-repelling coatings cut clotting in lab tests; no stent keeps its air layer in the body.
real: Superhydrophobic air-trapping surfaces resisted thrombosis in rabbit carotid tube implants and in ex vivo blood tests, and patents describe superhydrophobic stents, but no air-layer stent has been demonstrated in vivo.
